question: Which of the following enzymes breaks down starch into simple sugar?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Amylase.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Starch** is a **complex carbohydrate **that needs to be broken down into **simple sugars** for the body to use it as energy.
 
• **Amylase **is the enzyme responsible for breaking down starch into simple sugars like **glucose and maltose.**
 
• The majority of amylase in your body is produced by the **salivary glands and pancreas.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pepsin** is an enzyme produced in the** stomach.**

 
 
• It breaks down **proteins into amino acids.**
 
 
 
• **Trypsin** is an enzyme produced in the **pancreas**.
 
 
• It breaks down **proteins into smaller peptides.**
 
 
 
• **Lipase** is an enzyme that breaks down fats into **fatty acids and glycerol.**
